newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy rate cut seen sooner, bigger after CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Italy rate cut seen sooner, bigger after CPI data.

text.p: Italian economists said on Monday they expected the Bank of Italy to cut its key discount rate in the middle of next month, by up to a full percentage point, if final inflation data confirms preliminary October figures.

They said preliminary consumer price data from Milan, Trieste and Turin pointed to a year-on-year rate of 3.1 percent in October -- a level which could open the door to a rate cut if the government's 1997 budget clears the lower house of parliament on schedule by mid-November.
"We expect 75-100 basis points off the discount rate this time next month," Sharda Persaud, economist at San Paolo bank in London, told Reuters Financial Television.
The preliminary data from Milan and Trieste particularly impressed analysts. Milan came in with a year-on-year figure of 3.2 percent, compared with 4.0 percent in September.
Trieste's year-on-year rate was 2.7 percent against 3.0 percent in September, while Turin showed 2.8 percent versus 2.9 percent.
"It's favourable, just for the prospects in the short term for having a lower discount rate," Mario Noera, chief economist at Deutsche Bank, told RFTV after publication of the data.
"The Bank of Italy will probably cut (the discount rate) when inflation falls under three percent. The chances of having three percent inflation earlier than expected are increasing."
Lorenzo Codogno, head of research at Bank of America said he expected a full 100 basis point cut, with November the earliest available opportunity.

The Chamber of Deputies (lower house) is due to have finished debating Prime Minister Romano Prodi's 1997 austerity budget, which is designed to slash 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off next year's deficit, by November 17.

Economists said that could be a timely moment for a rate cut, since the budget then passes to the Senate (upper house), which Prodi's centre-left coalition controls. The budget must by law be passed by both houses of parliament by the year's end.

"I think a reduction in the discount rate could be more substantial than expected," Noera said, adding he was looking for a reduction of 75 to 100 basis points. "Later in November could be a good time for a rate cut," he said.
The Bank of Italy ended a 14-month freeze when it cut the discount rate to 8.25 percent from nine percent in July.

A Reuter quarterly poll of leading economists published last week pointed to an average forecast discount rate cut of 75 basis points to 7.50 percent by the end of this year and a further 25 basis point easing in the first quarter of 1997.
Seven other sample cities -- Naples, Palermo, Florence, Perugia, Venice, Bologna and Genoa -- publish preliminary CPI data on Tuesday.
Final official inflation data for October will be issued by the national statistics institute ISTAT on November 6. ($=1,531)
